article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Sunset Sherbet × Thin Mint GSC
Breeder: Cookie Fam Genetics / Sherbinskis and Jigga
THC Content: 20–25%
CBD Content: Generally below 1%
Terpene Profile: caryophyllene , limonene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Sweet cream, berry, citrus, mint, earth
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September through October
Indoor Yield: Medium to high
Outdoor Yield: Medium to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Before Gelato became one of the most copied names in modern cannabis, it was a room full of numbered plants in San Francisco. Gelato 25 was one of the selections that survived that original phenotype hunt, emerging from the same Sunset Sherbet × Thin Mint GSC population that produced famous relatives such as Gelato #33 and Bacio Gelato #41 . High Times identified #25 by the nickname Barry Bonds when documenting the standout Gelato phenotypes in 2016.

The strain combines dessert-like sweetness with a noticeably funkier underside than its name implies: cream and berry can give way to mint, citrus peel, damp earth, spice, and gasoline once the flowers are broken apart. Its high follows a similar contrast, beginning with an upbeat cerebral shift before settling into a heavier, more comfortable body effect. Gelato 25 also earned lasting importance as breeding material, most notably as a parent of Biscotti, proving that this comparatively rare phenotype influenced modern weed far beyond the jars that carried its own name.
Genetics and Lineage

Gelato 25 is not a separate cross made by breeding “Gelato” to another plant. It is one phenotype selected from the original Sunset Sherbet × Thin Mint Cookies breeding project created by Sherbinski and Jigga. Cannabis Now documented the project directly with Sherbinski, who explained that the numbered Gelato designations originated as the numbers placed on individual plants during selection. A large population was reduced through vigor and quality screening before the remaining phenotypes were evaluated for aroma, flowering traits, structure, and overall cannabis quality.

Sunset Sherbet contributes much of the fruit, cream, color, and softer physical character. Its own ancestry runs through the Cookies family , giving Gelato 25 a substantial dose of the dense flower structure and dessert aromatics that helped redefine California marijuana during the 2010s. Thin Mint GSC supplies another Cookies-derived influence but pushes the profile toward mint, fuel, earth, and sharper potency. The fact that both parents draw from closely related Bay Area genetics helps explain why the Gelato family can feel coherent even while individual numbered phenotypes smell and behave quite differently.

Gelato #25 later became especially important through Biscotti. Connected Cannabis identifies its original Biscotti as South Florida OG × Gelato #25 and states that it created the cross in 2016. That contribution helped extend #25 into another major branch of contemporary American genetics. The cultivar is sometimes called Barry Bonds, while “Guava Gelato” is occasionally attached to #25 as well; that latter alias is less dependable because Guava Gelato has also been used for unrelated plants. For accurate strain identification, Gelato #25 or Barry Bonds is the safer terminology.
Effects and Experience

The first few minutes often emphasize the brighter side of the hybrid. A noticeable cerebral lift may increase sociability, interest, and sensory engagement without immediately creating the frantic pace associated with highly stimulating Haze varieties. Conversation can feel easier, music becomes more absorbing, and an ordinary evening may suddenly seem considerably more entertaining. High Times described the original Gelato family as containing meaningful differences between phenotypes, which is important here—#25 should not be assumed to produce exactly the same experience as #33 or #41 simply because the parents are identical.

Relaxation gradually becomes more obvious as the initial mental energy levels out. The body may feel heavier through the arms and legs while the head remains pleasantly elevated, producing the balanced but indica-leaning character often associated with this selection. Moderate consumption can work well for music, movies, conversation, creative interests, or an unhurried evening. Larger amounts shift the balance considerably, bringing stronger appetite, reduced motivation, and a greater likelihood of settling into one place.

With flower commonly falling around the low-to-mid 20% THC range, this is not especially forgiving weed for someone with little tolerance. Too much can produce dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, anxious thinking, or a level of physical heaviness that overwhelms the more enjoyable cerebral phase. The original cut’s reputation comes from quality and balance rather than simply chasing the highest possible laboratory number.
Medical Benefits

Gelato 25 may appeal to medical marijuana consumers who want physical relaxation without an entirely dull or narcotic headspace. The initial euphoric component can make stress or low mood feel less dominant for some individuals, while the later physical effects may help shift attention away from everyday aches or muscular tension. Appetite stimulation can also become noticeable as the experience matures.

Its heavier second half makes afternoon and evening use more practical for many consumers than early-morning use. Higher doses can become considerably more relaxing and may encourage sleepiness, though that effect is neither guaranteed nor unique to this cultivar. The same THC concentration that feels calming to one patient can create anxiety or racing thoughts in another.

No clinical study has demonstrated that Gelato 25 itself treats anxiety, insomnia, chronic pain, depression, or another specific medical condition. Medical cannabis response depends on cannabinoids, dose, terpene composition, individual physiology, tolerance, and medication use. Patients should therefore evaluate the laboratory results of the actual product rather than treating the strain name as a prescription.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Sweetness comes first, but #25 is not pure candy. Cured flowers can open with cream, berry, and citrus before revealing a deeper combination of mint, soil, black pepper, and fuel. Contemporary descriptions of authentic or preserved material repeatedly emphasize a sweet-and-funky profile with fruit and spice underneath, while some examples lean more heavily toward creamy vanilla or earthy Cookies notes.

Grinding the buds usually brings the darker aromas forward. The mint becomes sharper, earth and fuel thicken, and the fruit can take on a more tart berry or citrus-peel quality. On the palate, cream and sweetness tend to appear early before a spicy, slightly gassy exhale. This layered transition is one reason Gelato genetics became so influential: the flowers can smell immediately approachable while still retaining enough funk to satisfy consumers who prefer traditional pungent cannabis.

Aggregated laboratory data for modern Gelato 25 products commonly finds limonene and beta-caryophyllene among the stronger terpenes, with myrcene, humulene, linalool, and pinene appearing behind them. Those ratios should not be treated as mandatory markers of authenticity. Environment, harvest timing, phenotype preservation, drying, and storage can all reshape the terpene profile of finished marijuana.
Growing Information

The original Gelato family was selected partly on cultivation performance, not flavor alone. Sherbinski specifically discussed evaluating Gelato plants for traits including rapid development, flowering behavior, structure, and suitability for restricted vertical spaces. Gelato 25 generally carries that indoor-oriented architecture, developing into a medium-sized plant with relatively dense flowers and substantial resin rather than extreme sativa stretch.

Flowering usually falls within the broader Gelato window of approximately eight to ten weeks, a range also documented by High Times for the original strain family. Plants benefit from an even canopy because closely spaced flowering sites can shade lower growth once the upper flowers begin swelling. Moderate early training can help spread the branches and improve light penetration without requiring aggressive manipulation.

Density is the main late-flower concern. Thick Cookies-style buds can trap moisture when the interior canopy is crowded, so airflow and controlled humidity become increasingly important during the final weeks. Growers should also expect substantial aroma as resin production intensifies. Carbon filtration may be worthwhile indoors where odor control matters.

Reliable original breeder yield numbers for the #25 phenotype are not widely documented, so exaggerated gram-per-square-meter figures should be treated cautiously. A medium-to-high yield is realistic under strong indoor conditions, but #25 became valuable primarily because of flower quality, resin, flavor, and breeding potential rather than because it was known as a record-setting commercial producer.
FAQ
What is Gelato 25?

Gelato 25 is one of the original numbered phenotypes selected from the Sunset Sherbet × Thin Mint GSC Gelato breeding project created by Sherbinski and Jigga. It is also commonly known as Barry Bonds.
Is Gelato 25 the same as regular Gelato?

Gelato 25 belongs to the original Gelato family, but it is one specific phenotype rather than a separate generic version of Gelato. Other famous selections include Gelato #33, Gelato #41, and Gelato #45.
What are the genetics of Gelato 25?
The lineage is Sunset Sherbet × Thin Mint Girl Scout Cookies. High Times documented #25 among the original keeper phenotypes from that cross in 2016.
What does Gelato 25 taste like?
Expect sweet cream, berry, citrus, and mint layered with earth, pepper, and gasoline. Some examples lean strongly toward creamy dessert flavors, while others show more Cookies-style funk.
How long does Gelato 25 take to flower?
Approximately eight to ten weeks indoors is a reasonable flowering window. Individual cuts and cultivation environments can shift maturity by several days.
Final Thoughts on Gelato 25

Gelato 25 matters because it represents the original Gelato story before the name became attached to countless crosses and imitations. Sherbinski and Jigga created a large Sunset Sherbet × Thin Mint Cookies population, numbered the plants, and selected distinct expressions rather than reducing everything to a single winner. #25 survived that process alongside several phenotypes that would go on to become some of the most famous cannabis cuts of the decade.

Its personality is unmistakably modern California: sweet cream and fruit on the surface, Cookies funk and gasoline underneath, dense resinous buds, and an effect that mixes cerebral euphoria with substantial body relaxation. Yet its importance extends beyond what the flower tastes like. As a parent of Biscotti, Gelato #25 helped establish another major family of contemporary marijuana genetics.

For a serious strain library , it is therefore best understood not simply as “another Gelato.” Gelato 25 is a specific historic phenotype—Barry Bonds—from the original Cookie Fam Gelato project. That combination of documented pedigree, phenotype-selection history, dessert-meets-fuel flavor, balanced potency, and major breeding influence gives it a distinct place in modern cannabis genetics.
